clips.name: Annville arrival · LVC to the Christmas house
JESS: Mom, I'm sorry. I can't come home for Christmas this year. Work is crazy.
JESS: Mom? Is that a siren?
LINDA: Don't worry, sweetheart. I think it's for me.
JESS: My mom's in the hospital. Two days. I'll be back in two days, I promise.
JESS: I don't really fit here anymore. Everyone still thinks I'm seventeen.
JESS: I know, but things will be better in the new year, when this project finishes. And yes, I'll be there for the New Year's Eve party.
JESS: Mom, you were in an ambulance!
LINDA: It's just a sprain. The neighbors called an ambulance.
JESS: I'm charging now. Send me the revisions. I'll look at them on the way.
JESS: Please tell me you’re open.
BEN: For you, or the car?
BEN: The plow bent your rear suspension. You can’t drive it like this.
BEN: The part gets here December twenty-ninth.
JESS: The twenty-ninth? I promised I'd be back for New Year's Eve.
BEN: Well, you’re not going anywhere today.
JESS: Wait. Do I know you?
BEN: Ben Kreider. You borrowed my truck for the homecoming parade.
JESS: Any news on the part?
JESS: In the city, I never get to see the sun go down. It's just gone by four o'clock.
BEN: Stay a while. It's worth the wait.
BEN: Don't get attached. She'll be gone the minute that car is fixed.
JESS: Is that really what you think of me?
BEN: Jess, wait. That's not what I meant.
PA VOLUNTEER: Okay, folks! Let's light this tree!
LINDA: Dot, her car's been ready since Tuesday.
LINDA: And she still hasn't left.
